questions.prompt: What is the time complexity of building a heap from n elements bottom-up (heapify)?
questions.explanation: Bottom-up build-heap is O(n): most nodes are near the bottom and sift down only a little, and the total sift work sums to O(n).

questions.prompt: What is the cost of extracting the minimum from a min-heap of n elements?
questions.explanation: Removing the root moves the last element up and sifts it down along one root-to-leaf path — O(log n). Only peeking (not removing) is O(1).

questions.prompt: Which statements about binary heaps are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: A heap is a complete binary tree stored in an array
heappush and heappop are O(log n)
Building a heap from an existing array is O(n)

questions.explanation: Heaps are array-backed complete trees with O(log n) push/pop and O(n) construction. Heapsort is in-place but NOT stable.

questions.prompt: Python's heapq module implements a ______-heap. (min or max)
questions.explanation: heapq is a min-heap; for max-heap behaviour you negate the values or use heapq.nlargest.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to pop the minimum from a min-heap.

items.text: Take the root as the result (the minimum)
Move the last element into the root position
Sift the new root down until the heap property holds

questions.explanation: Record the root, replace it with the last element to keep the tree complete, then sift down to restore the heap property.

questions.prompt: Match each heap operation with its time complexity.
questions.explanation: Peeking the root is constant; push/pop sift along one path (log n); constructing from an array is linear.
